classification.difficultyReason: Solve linear absolute value equations by two cases and check against supplied sketches; the final two parts require rearrangement.

content.prompt: Solve these equations. Use the sketches to check your answer.

spec.description: Supplied upward V, unit grid, labelled horizontal ticks −4 to 4 excluding zero and vertical ticks 1 to 8.

answer.worked:
For $2x-1\geq0$:
$$\begin{aligned}2x-1&=3\\2x&=4\\x&=2\end{aligned}$$
For $2x-1<0$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(2x-1)&=3\\-2x+1&=3\\-2x&=2\\x&=-1\end{aligned}$$
Both satisfy their cases. The supplied curve meets $y=3$ at $(-1,3)$ and $(2,3)$, confirming the answers.

spec.description: Supplied upward V; horizontal grid step 1, vertical grid step 2; all source tick labels retained.

answer.worked:
For $3-2x\geq0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3-2x&=5\\-2x&=2\\x&=-1\end{aligned}$$
For $3-2x<0$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(3-2x)&=5\\-3+2x&=5\\2x&=8\\x&=4\end{aligned}$$
Both satisfy their cases. The supplied curve meets $y=5$ at $(-1,5)$ and $(4,5)$, confirming the answers.

spec.description: Supplied upward V; horizontal grid step 2, vertical grid step 4; horizontal labels −8 to 8 excluding zero.

answer.worked:
For $3x+5\geq0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3x+5&=16\\3x&=11\\x&=\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}$$
For $3x+5<0$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(3x+5)&=16\\-3x-5&=16\\-3x&=21\\x&=-7\end{aligned}$$
Both satisfy their cases. The supplied curve meets $y=16$ at $(-7,16)$ and $\left(\frac{11}{3},16\right)$, confirming the answers.

spec.description: Supplied upward V; horizontal grid step 1 and vertical grid step 2.

answer.worked:
For $1-2x\geq0$:
$$\begin{aligned}1-2x&=5\\-2x&=4\\x&=-2\end{aligned}$$
For $1-2x<0$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(1-2x)&=5\\-1+2x&=5\\2x&=6\\x&=3\end{aligned}$$
Both satisfy their cases. The supplied curve meets $y=5$ at $(-2,5)$ and $(3,5)$, confirming the answers.

spec.description: Supplied downward V on a unit grid, horizontal labels −7 to 7 and vertical labels −5 to 5, excluding zero.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}-|2x+1|+5&=3\\-|2x+1|&=-2\\|2x+1|&=2\end{aligned}$$
For $2x+1\geq0$:
$$\begin{aligned}2x+1&=2\\2x&=1\\x&=\frac12\end{aligned}$$
For $2x+1<0$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(2x+1)&=2\\-2x-1&=2\\-2x&=3\\x&=-\frac32\end{aligned}$$
Both satisfy their cases. The supplied curve meets $y=3$ at $\left(-\frac32,3\right)$ and $\left(\frac12,3\right)$, confirming the answers.

spec.description: Supplied upward V on a unit grid, horizontal labels −7 to 7 and vertical labels −5 to 5, excluding zero.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}|x+1|-3&=0\\|x+1|&=3\end{aligned}$$
For $x+1\geq0$:
$$\begin{aligned}x+1&=3\\x&=2\end{aligned}$$
For $x+1<0$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(x+1)&=3\\-x-1&=3\\-x&=4\\x&=-4\end{aligned}$$
Both satisfy their cases. The supplied curve crosses $y=0$ at $(-4,0)$ and $(2,0)$, confirming the answers.
